# Concept Map — Melting

## Source and scope
Adapts the version-pinned synthetic public-domain article **Synthetic Handbook of Melting (fixture-only)**.

## Summary
Melting of a pure solid at standard pressure, and the energy it absorbs.

## Prerequisites
- Temperature and thermal energy

## Objectives
1. State the melting point of pure water at standard pressure.
2. Explain why the temperature stays constant while a pure solid melts.

## Concept sequence
1. A pure solid melts at a characteristic temperature.
2. Energy absorbed during melting does not raise the temperature.

## Key terms
- **melting point** (fusion point, aliases: melting temperature) — the temperature at which a pure solid becomes liquid [concept.melting.1]
- **latent heat of fusion** (heat of fusion) — the energy absorbed while a solid melts [concept.melting.2]

## Misconceptions to surface
- Temperature always rises when heat is added to a solid.
